standard_prerequisites.name: The level predicate
standard_prerequisites.statement: is-type n of X is the type expressing that X is an n-type, defined by recursion on the level with the contractibility predicate at the bottom.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the predicate whose propositionality is proved.

standard_prerequisites.name: Level of a product of propositions
standard_prerequisites.statement: A product of mere propositions is a mere proposition, and a level predicate over a path type is an instance of that.
standard_prerequisites.use: It reduces the inductive step to a pointwise statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: Contractibility is a proposition
standard_prerequisites.statement: For every type X the type is-contr(X) is a mere proposition.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the base case of the induction.

core_obligations: Prove the statement by induction on the level n (source line 194).
Base case: the contractibility predicate is a mere proposition, which is the cited result (source lines 196-197).

Inductive step: assume the level predicate is a mere proposition for n and show it for the successor level, which reduces to showing that a product of level predicates over a path type is a mere proposition (source lines 199-202).

Use the product case of propositionality (or equivalently the level of a product) to reduce further to the level predicate over a single path type, and apply the induction hypothesis to that path type (source lines 203-205).

proof_roadmap.step: Induction on the level, with the contractibility base case.
The successor step, reduced to a product over path types.
Reduce to one path type and apply the induction hypothesis.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled theorem at source lines 190-192 (book Theorem 7.1.10): for every level n at least minus two and every type X, the type is-type n of X is a mere proposition. The statement is a propositionality claim about a predicate defined by recursion, and the proof (source lines 193-206) has to run that induction: the base case is the propositionality of the contractibility predicate, and the successor step moves the claim one level up the path hierarchy, where the goal becomes a product of level predicates over the path type; only after reducing that product to its factors, using the product case of propositionality, does the induction hypothesis apply. The reduction of the product to a single path type is the step the statement hides.
